title: Corn, NS as to form, cooked

content.title: About
content.content: Corn (Zea mays) is an annual cereal plant cultivated worldwide. Cooked corn on the cob has a sweet flavor, juicy texture, and bright yellow color. It is commonly served as a side dish or used in salads, soups, and Asian-inspired recipes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn is one of the most important food crops, grown in over 100 countries.
There are more than 300 varieties of corn, differing in size, color, and taste.
Sweet corn, which is usually boiled, contains more sugar than field corn varieties.
Corn was domesticated in Mexico more than 7,000 years ago.
Corn kernels are used to produce starch, oil, and bio‑fuel.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber supports healthy digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C acts as an antioxidant, supports the immune system, and enhances iron absorption.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Provides magnesium and potassium
items.content: These minerals help regulate muscle and nerve function and maintain normal blood pressure.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Cooked corn provides about 90 kcal per 100 g, making it a good option for weight management.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn, ranging from skin rashes to respiratory issues.

items.title: High carbohydrate content
items.content: Corn has a relatively high glycemic index, so people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Phytic acid presence
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce the absorption of certain minerals; soaking or sprouting lowers its level.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boil corn on the cob in salted water for 5‑7 minutes until tender. It can be eaten plain, added to salads, soups, chili, or used as a filling for tacos and burritos. Grilling the cob adds a smoky flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh ears in the refrigerator in a plastic bag for 3‑5 days. Frozen ears retain quality for up to 8 months when stored in an airtight container.
